dedupe_keys.name: china covid 19 medical waste dataset and city level disposal optimisation for 343 cities

description: This case study compiles a city-level dataset of the medical waste generated in China during the COVID-19 pandemic and the capacity available to dispose of it, and uses it to derive disposal strategies for future outbreaks. The authors, from Tsinghua University's School of Environment, published it as a resource article in Nature Sustainability. They developed a model estimating daily medical waste from respiratory disease outbreaks through the test, isolation and treatment chain across 343 Chinese cities, analysed waste patterns under different stages of restriction measures, and assessed the sustainability of medical waste management. Coverage is 343 cities in China. The article is behind a subscription paywall; the terms for the dataset are not stated on the page read. Caveats: estimates depend on modelled waste generation rates per test, patient and isolation, disposal capacity data come from official reporting, and the article's full methods were not read here. The authors identify city-specific disposal optimisation strategies and state that the dataset and model can support further research and help policy makers manage medical waste in future emergencies. Simulation uses: estimating surges in medical waste and disposal capacity shortfalls in pandemic emergency response and capacity planning. Related records: the healthcare waste management study in 14 countries (case_study-healthcare-waste-management-14-lmics) covers routine facility waste services.
